series: Before Launching Your Cosmetics Brand in Korea
approvedBy: Draft for comparison — not approved for publication

cards.headline: Can a Company Representative Be the Manager?
body: A representative must qualify, even with 10 or fewer regular employees.
cards.takeaway: With 10 or fewer regular employees, a qualified representative may perform the manager's duties.
cards.design: Premium navy editorial cover with an oversized 10 and one document motif. Separate series No.02 from page 1/10. No floating shapes, mockups or 3D objects.

cards.headline: Two Conditions for Representative Dual Duty

body.text: The business must have 10 or fewer regular employees. A small workforce does not waive manager qualifications.
The proprietor or corporate representative needs a listed qualification and must actually perform the duties.

cards.takeaway: Both requirements must hold. Headcount alone is not enough.
cards.design: Editorial side-by-side comparison emphasizing the 10-person threshold and personal qualification, using thin dividers and deliberate negative space.

cards.headline: More Than One Way to Qualify

body.text: Science, engineering or another listed bachelor's field.
Listed associate degree and 1 year of post-degree quality work.
At least 2 years in cosmetics manufacturing or quality control.

cards.takeaway: Doctors and pharmacists also qualify; special training covers only designated products.
cards.design: Four typographic qualifications routes in one grid. Treat 1 year after graduation and 2 years of work as different legal paths, not as a proportional chart.

cards.headline: How Does the MFDS Assess a Degree?
body: The MFDS generally checks science or engineering degree or academic-track wording on official certificates.
This is a paraphrase, not a direct quotation. The regional MFDS office reviews the actual documents to determine individual eligibility.
cards.takeaway: Check the awarded degree and field shown on official records.
cards.design: An editorial agency-guidance extract that clearly marks paraphrase versus agency source. Avoid simulated official seals, stamps or invented paperwork.

cards.headline: Same Two Years. Different Qualifying Work.

body.text: Hypothetical A reviewed quality records for at least 2 years. The duties and period must be proven.
Hypothetical B handled advertising and sales for 2 years, not cosmetics manufacturing or quality control.

cards.takeaway: Two years in the industry is not automatically two years of qualifying work.
cards.design: Two fictional work certificates with identical periods and contrasting duties; label each Hypothetical, no copied seals or fabricated employers.

cards.headline: If the Representative Does Not Qualify
body: Check the representative's degree and actual work experience.
Review existing employees' degrees, experience and exam results.
If nobody qualifies, appoint an eligible working manager.
Define duties and the OEM manufacturer's document flow.
cards.takeaway: Appoint someone who can carry out the duties—not merely lend their name.
cards.design: A four-step numbered vertical process with alternating typography weights. Keep line art and separators restrained, avoiding decorative arrows or portraits.

cards.headline: Four Checks Before Filing Registration
body: Does the diploma state the degree and relevant field?
Does proof of work show relevant duties and dates?
Does dual duty meet both the 10-person limit and qualification rule?
Can this manager oversee quality and post-sale safety?
cards.takeaway: Compare the statutory route with the proof you have—not job titles alone.
cards.design: A practical saved-reference checklist with four legible questions and a restrained editorial document grid, not four oversized decorative boxes.

cards.headline: Qualifications and Actual Duties Come First.
cards.takeaway: A manager must qualify under the rules and actually perform the required work.
cards.design: Navy typography-only interlude with generous negative space. No ornaments or illustrations; emphasize Actual Duties.

cards.headline: Three Different Deadlines After Appointment

body.text: Initial training: within 6 months of starting duties, with an exam exception.
Refresher training: annually from the first training date.
Change of manager: register within 30 days, as a rule.

cards.takeaway: Different duties, different starting dates: track each one separately.
cards.design: Three large independent numeric deadlines, each with its own starting event. Never use comparable bar lengths because the units differ.

cards.headline: Review the Evidence Before You Appoint

body.text: Degrees or work certificates, entity information, workforce size and the proposed manager's duties.
Check the qualifying route, dual-duty conditions and whether more evidence or another qualified manager is needed.

cards.takeaway: ETHOS Administrative Attorney Office offers a free preliminary eligibility review.
cards.design: Calm professional-services editorial layout, two columns for source materials and preliminary assessment. No link, QR code, form or promotional button.
